subject: Identify clonal genotypes from a dataset

messages.author: 117cbc630cbf3340
messages.subject: Identify clonal genotypes from a dataset
parts:
Dear all,

Does anyone know if there is a function to identify clonal genotypes from a dataset in dartR?

I am just worried that these clonal genotypes might be skewing the allele frequencies and Fst values.

I would really appreciate your help on this matter,

Thanks in advance

-
Simon

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Identify clonal genotypes from a dataset
parts:
Hi Simon,

We don't have a function specifically for identifying clones, but you can use the function to calculate the proportion of shared alleles between individuals: gl.propShared().
If you have clones in your dataset, pairs of individuals should have a very high value, say more than 99%.

Here is some example code for this approach.

library(dartR)
# calculating the proportion of shared alleles
res <- gl.propShared(platypus.gl)
# converting a matrix into columns 
clones_temp <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(res)))
# filtering individuals using a threshold of 0.99
clones_temp_2 <- clones_temp[clones_temp$Freq>0.99,]
# getting pairs of individuals that are not the same
clones <- clones_temp_2[which(clones_temp_2$Var1!=clones_temp_2$Var2),]

To have more security in the results, I would recommend that you eliminate the loci that have missing data using a very conservative threshold, for example: gl.filter.callrate(platypus.gl,threshold = 1)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Identify clonal genotypes from a dataset
parts:
Hi Simon,

 

Not sure if that helps. Below is a script I developed with a colleague looking in the reproduction modes in ferns.

 

The genlight object (fern.catch) has populations and I compare within each population the individuals and there genotypes.

 

The output is the number of mismatches for clones, selfing and parent-offsprings between pairs of individuals in a population.

 

So you should get the clones by looking at the mismatches in the clonemm column (there might be a few due to genotyping errors so you need to define a threshold, when you call a clone).

 

The other mismatches indentify selfing and parent-offspring relationship, but are naturally less precise (we do not know the parents).

 

The output is a list that has a data.frame for  each population. So if you do not have population simply define a single population for your genlight object.

 

 

Hope that helps,

 

Cheers, Bernd

 

 

 

 

#compare within catchments

pops <- seppop(fern.catch)

 

#check mismatches

 

res <- list()

 

for (ii in 1:length(pops))

{

pp <- pops[[ii]]

m <- as.matrix(pp)

#allpairs

cb <- t(combn(nInd(pp),2))

 

df <- data.frame(nind1=cb[,1], nind2=cb[,2], ind1=indNames(pp)[cb[,1]], ind2=indNames(pp)[cb[,2]], nloc=NA, clonemm =NA, selfmm=NA, pomm=NA, clonemmp=NA, selfmmp=NA, pommp=NA)

 

nl <- nLoc(pp)

 

for (i in 1:nrow(df))

{

                i1 <- m[df$nind1[i], ]

                i2 <- m[df$nind2[i], ]

               

                miss <- is.na(i1) | is.na(i2)

                i1c <- i1[!miss]

                i2c <- i2[!miss]

                ncom <- nl-sum(miss)

                #cloning mismatches

                cmm <- sum(i1c!=i2c)

               

                #selfing missmatches

                smm <- sum(i1c==0 & i2c!=0) + sum(i1c==2 & i2c!=2)

               

                #po missmatches

  pomm <- sum(i1c==0 & i2c==2)+ sum(i1c==2 & i2c==0)

                df[i,5:11]<- c(ncom, cmm, smm, pomm, cmm/ncom, smm/ncom, pomm/ncom)

}

 

res[[ii]] <- df

}

 

names(res)<- names(pops)

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Identify clonal genotypes from a dataset
parts:
Dear Luis, Bernd and Peter,

Thank you so much for your advice in this regard,

The three approaches retrieved consistent results in identifying clonal genotypes in my dataset.

Actually, I included four replicates samples per plate, and all of them were identified in each analysis. These replicates were useful to establish a threshold, specifically for methods 1 (Luis) and 2 (Bernd). In relation to approach three (Peter), the clones had small branches and shared the same node.

I was just worried about clonal reproduction in some of my target species. 

So, thank you so much for your help and advice.

Kind regards,
--
Simón
